newsitem.title: GERMANY: German building outlook hurt by limited investment.
newsitem.headline: German building outlook hurt by limited investment.

text.p: The German construction industry should see investment fall another 2.2 percent in 1997 as the government pares spending and commercial investors fret about economic growth, a builders group said on Friday.

The Association of the German Construction Industry (HDB) said orders in the first two months of the year were down 7.5 percent compared to the same 1996 period, hurt in particular by a 23.7 percent fall in public construction in eastern Germany.
"The construction industry downturn has not let up at the beginning of the year," the group said in a statement.
But economists said the two-year construction slump could ease in 1998.

"We are estimating a small, one-percent increase in investment next year," said Hermann Remsperger at BHF Bank in Frankfurt. "It's no great growth, but commercial investment should be a bit stronger."

The HDB investment outlook nearly matches earlier projections from the government and another industry organisation. In March Bonn estimated building investment would fall three percent this year, while the ZDB building employers' group forecast a 2.5 percent drop.
HDB said investment was expected to decline 1.4 percent in western Germany, and 4.1 percent in eastern Germany.
In the first two months of 1997, orders in western Germany were down a real 6.9 percent due to a 12.1 percent fall in commercial construction.
"Companies have held back with the economic outlook relatively limited," Remsperger said.
West German orders in home and public works construction fell 3.8 percent and 0.8 percent, respectively.
East German orders in January and February dropped 9.2 percent as public construction orders plunged after the government cut special tax incentives for the former communist region.
Bonn has pared back spending broadly in an effort to meet the criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
Commercial construction in the east dropped 14.6 percent, but was partially offset by a 9.2 percent gain in orders for homes, HDB said.
The industry employed an average of 1.1 million workers in the two-month period, down 120,000, or 9.7 percent, from the same period in 1996.

For all of 1997, the group said average construction employment was seen falling to 1.2 million, down six percent from the level last year. It expected east German payrolls to decline 9 percent to 380,000 workers, and west German payrolls to fall five percent to 852,000.
